To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the core spliceosome component, PRPF8, is a limiting factor in splice site recognition and splicing fidelity.
PRPF8 is a limiting component of the core spliceosome, whose availability determines constitutive and alternative RNA splicing across the transcriptome.
the core spliceosome factor PRPF8 is a rate-limiting component for the splicing of RNPs with weak 5’ splice sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of human genetic disorders, and how changes in the core machinery of the spliceosome can affect the expression of human genes.
the molecular mechanisms of RNA splicing in human cells and how these processes are affected in human diseases.
the regulation of alternative splicing by the core spliceosome component, PRPF8.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PRPF8 is an important regulator of alternative splicing and is involved in the regulation of constitutive splicing.
PRPF8 is a key regulator of splicing, and the strength of 5′ splice signals is the major determinant of PRPF8-dependent splicing regulation.
PRPF8 deficiency leads to a decrease in RNP complex formation and that this leads to the retention of weak 5′ introns and that this in turn leads to mitotic arrest.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PRPF8 is a key component of the core spliceosome, and that the strength of the 5′ splice-site is a key determinant of the efficiency of splicing in the human genome.
the splicing of weak 5′ splicing sites is more sensitive to changes in core spliceosome abundance than strong splice sites.
the splicing of intron-containing genes with weak 5’ splice sites are most affected in the absence of PRPF8.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the splicing of weak 5′ splicing sites is sensitive to PRPF8 depletion.
weak 5′ splicing sites are a major determinant for the effects of PRFP8 deficiency on splicing.
the splicing of weak splice sites is more sensitive to PRPF8 availability, and that PRPF8 availability is more important in the context of weak splice sites than strong splice sites.
